rationale: C03 plausibly supplied a material template: both letters refer to a report produced following the President's request, acknowledge its receipt and implications, assign continued follow-up work, and request further recommendations or progress reports from time to time. C18 shares the report-acknowledgment and future-report elements but lacks the distinctive prior-request and continuing-assignment sequence. C12 likewise records receipt of a requested report and directs further action, but its statutory strike-injunction machinery is substantially different.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the informative report ... which you prepared at my request and submitted to me
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I requested Mr. Gordon Gray to undertake a comprehensive study ... Mr. Gray has now submitted his report.
shared_material.explanation: Both establish that the President previously commissioned work and has now received the resulting report.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I would therefore appreciate it if you continued to follow the matter for me.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This is a special task which I am asking the Advisory Board to undertake for me
shared_material.explanation: Both use receipt of the report as the basis for assigning continued or additional work on the subject.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Please advise me of developments and report your recommendations from time to time
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I know you will apprise me from time to time as to how the work is proceeding.
shared_material.explanation: The closely parallel request for periodic updates is distinctive shared drafting language and function.
